items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: like the Alden-Barrett quintet, that set we just did a few minutes ago.

ctx.x: Well not really being a student of the history you know, I don’t know why. And I don’t know why bands will work one night and not another, I’m talking about the same band. Some things are so much better. Somebody said to Miles Davis one night, said, “Man, you sound beautiful tonight.” And Miles said, “Well maybe you’re just listening good tonight. Maybe you’re having a good night.” And I mean so his point was maybe it sounds good to you because you’re in a good place. And when an audience, when you get enough…

really goes wrong. Did you ever put a record, a needle down in the middle of a record, or flip on the radio in the middle of a jazz chorus and you don’t know what planet these people are on. A lot of times non-players — I’d love to know what they hear. So the funny thing is when something is really, really good they know it. If it’s bad — something wasn’t quite right. Yeah the drummer was in five-four all night. They don’t know that. But they’re not sure why it isn’t working real well. But when something, like…
Well that’s a great statement about his entertainment value as well as his talent. But when you said bebop mentality—
